questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A country were people spoke English, and an academically strong university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall it was a positive experience looking back.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy to find the needed information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They are very good at answering their email regarding any questions you have. However, the response time can be a couple of days. You have to figure out a lot yourself, a big one being housing, however they do have "good tips", that I did not use.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Pretty mediocre. They look at you only academically. There wasn't that many events for socializing hosted by the university, and you have to be the one taking the initiative.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It is very tough to find housing in Toronto. The market is pretty terrible for renters. My top tips:
If you want to be certain, and have the 'secure' way: use AirBnB or similair sites. If you are early you can quite often get prices that are similair to what renting would be anyways. Also they give a lot of security in case of issues with the landlord.
If you want to look at things when arriving do checkout
kijiji.com
. It is basically the same as dba here in Denmark, and it is where I found my accomidation after staying at a hostel for the first 2 weeks. This option is very tough though, as most Landlords want a 12-month lease agreement if not more.
If I had to do it over, I would use airbnb, and do it early. Just scout the site way in advance, and if you see a good deal, then go for it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A lot of people don't really have kitchen utilities and just buy takeout all the time. So if you like to cook your own food, keep that in mind.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There was next to no help from the university, and the dorms are very oversubscribed and not that available to exchange students.

Checkout Tartu College, I knew a few there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a computer science student the courses were very oversubscribed. They had good time planners, but if you don't get a course, then it doesn't matter how much you planned before.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You get the course list and a timetable builder. Then you have to fill out a google forms with the courses you'd like.

Also note, that you can search for as many courses as you would like, and they will give you at most 5. So I would recommend searching a ton of courses in round 1, making sure that they are interchangeable, and then drop one course if needed later on.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Timetable builder and course list. The course descriptions are quite short, which is a shame.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 6/10. As computer science was very oversubscribed I wasn't able to get all the course I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to study something in Computer Science, I would highly recommend Operating Systems and Kuei (Jack) Sun as a professor. He is brilliant, and the course is very interesting. However, it is also a very tough course, and you should be prepared to spend a lot of time on the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some courses (CSC236 especially) had more of a focus on given you a bunch of assignments/tests rather than teaching you the material. It seems that focus is more placed upon you spending countless hours on the study, rather than you understanding the material. Also note that everything you do is graded (down to surveys about how you feel about the course).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The course material is similar if not easier than what is offered at the University of Copenhagen for the same year.

However, their emphasis is placed more on you doing a bunch of work, rather than you knowing the course material. The grading also reflects this, as a minor mistake with the correct methodology usually ranks lower than the correct result with incorrect methodology.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I preferred UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CSC236, CSC207, APM236, CSC369

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: CSC369 - a tough course, but very interesting

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing is very expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I bought the bikeshare Tangerine annual membership. This costs 120cad for the version I bought. However, I used this as my primary way of getting around, which saved me a lot, as I feel the public transport is quite bad in Toronto. Mainly due to the trams using the same lanes as cars, and there is a lot of traffic in Toronto. So unless you live next to one of the two subway lines I would recommend just using the bike.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of sports clubs that you can sign up for, but you are not guaranteed to get in. There are also athletic centres were you can workout. However, I lived in a condo, which had a decently well equipped gym, so I mainly used that one.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Athletic mainly. Unlike Danish universities, there is not a lot of emphasis on the students socializing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you enjoy some specific sport, there is most likely a team that you can sign up for.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: As I was pretty swarmed with studies I didn't get to travel as much as I would've liked. However, I would have loved to visit some of the nature there is in Canada. My main regret is not going to see Banf national park.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty seamless. However, there is a lot more homelessness and drugs, which is quite unusual.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
People talk to randomly a lot more than in Denmark. Most people won't second guess it, if you just start talking to them, so do that!

However, my best tip is to just create a post in the UofT inbound exchange facebook group explaining your interest, and you might find a group of friends to hangout with with that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Homelessness and drug use. It is quite common to see people on some hard drugs walking down the streets. After having visited both New York and Toronto, I would say Toronto is even worse, even though it has been quite a few years since I was in New York.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People being open to talking. If you overhear some conversation during class, most people are open to you just joining in.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find housing early, my tip Airbnb.
Search a bunch of courses in the first round, such that if you don't get in, you have something to fallback on.
Figure out if you are going to prioritize the academics or social beforehand, and choose courses after that choice. There is a lot of variation in how much work a course takes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you can, try to find a place to live near campus. It is not quite downtown, but it will most likely be where you spend the most amount of time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying something different. I was getting quite comfortable in my own shoes here in Denmark, and enjoyed trying something different.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The personal relations you leave back home, and trying to keep in contact.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
